question: The resolution curriculum is now the main source of savings. E040 (24→32 px) cut ~3%, E047 (20 px first stage) ~3.5%, and E048 (24→28→32) brought the tip to 5.00 s. Two attempts failed: moving low-res steps later in training (E043) and adding a 28 px stage without the head-lr margin (E044). Both lost ~0.3-0.4 pp. Every other recent lever has been flat: head lr x3 (E049), Muon lr at bs 1536 (E046), and brightness/contrast jitter (E042). The question is how to schedule image resolution in a short, from-scratch CNN run so that more of the 3.75 full-res epochs can move to cheaper low-res steps without losing accuracy. Four sub-questions: (1) Should regularization or augmentation strength (translate, jitter, label smoothing) scale with resolution, as in EfficientNetV2-style progressive learning? (2) How should batch size and lr change across resolution stages? (3) How short can the final full-res stage be while still correcting the train/test resolution discrepancy (FixRes), for example with BN re-adaptation on training data or a short full-res tail? (4) Do smooth resolution ramps beat step schedules?

rubric: Gives a concrete resolution schedule (stage boundaries, sizes, or a ramp shape) for training from scratch, and reports accuracy at matched accuracy or matched wall-clock/FLOPs against fixed-resolution training.
Says how other hyperparameters (augmentation/regularization strength, batch size, lr) should change with resolution, or measures how they interact.
Measures how long or what kind of final full-resolution phase is needed to remove the train/test resolution gap (e.g. tail length, BN statistics re-estimation on training data).
Has evidence in a short-budget or small-image regime (CIFAR-scale, ResNet-style CNNs, few epochs) rather than only long ImageNet runs.
exclude: Methods that need pretrained weights, external data, or distillation from a pretrained teacher
Test-time augmentation, multi-resolution test ensembles, or any tuning or adaptation that uses test-set images (including BN adaptation on test data)
Fine-tuning at test resolution that uses data other than the 50,000 CIFAR-100 training images
Methods that need packages beyond PyTorch 2.4 / torchvision 0.19, or hardware features the A100 lacks (e.g. FP8)
Pure ViT/transformer patch-size or token-dropping methods that do not transfer to a small conv net
Results only reported for long (>=90-epoch) ImageNet schedules with no short-budget analysis
